desc: Parse input and check if any bad interval has length >= B; if so, output "No" and terminate.
Implement B-bit state vector where bit i indicates reachability of current square minus i, and build base transition out-masks for a good square: out[i] includes bit i+1 and bit 0 if A-1 <= i <= B-1.
Precompute powers of the transition matrix under Boolean composition (OR of out-masks) up to about 40 levels.
Implement apply_power(state, L) using binary exponentiation and matrix-vector multiplication via out-masks.

Process the line from square 1 to N: initialize state=1 at position 1; for each bad interval, apply the preceding good run with apply_power, then left-shift the state by the interval length; after all intervals, apply the final good run to N.
Output "Yes" if the lowest bit of the final state is 1, otherwise "No".
Test against the three provided samples and edge cases (M=0, A=B, blocking interval, N up to 1e12).
